---
request: Competitive analysis of our docs tool against Notion and Confluence for mid-size engineering teams.
---
Verdict

Compete on speed of search and on price for teams under 200 seats; do not compete on breadth of features, where both rivals lead.

Competitors

Notion: $10 per seat per month on the Plus plan; target customer is cross-functional startup teams; strongest feature is flexible pages and databases; weakest point is search across large workspaces; momentum is high. Confluence: $6.05 per seat per month on Standard; target customer is enterprises already on Jira; strongest feature is Jira integration; weakest point is page speed; momentum is flat.

| Company | Price | Target customer | Strength | Weakness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Notion | $10 | Startup teams | Flexible pages | Search at scale |
| Confluence | $6.05 | Jira enterprises | Jira integration | Page speed |

Pricing

Notion Plus is $10 per seat per month; Confluence Standard is $6.05. We are at $8, between them.

Where we lose

We have no database views and no offline mode; both rivals have one or the other.

Switching costs

A team moving from Confluence loses its Jira links unless we import them; that is the first thing a buyer will ask.

Risks

Confluence could cut its price for small teams. Recommendation: lead with search speed and a Confluence importer that keeps Jira links.
